searchText: The exit epoch & withdrawal epoch are separate. We could exit immediately & keep the normal withdrawal delay. What "bounded legacy slashing window" value do you have in mind here? Like 4096 epochs or is that too long? Ah I see, I need to think through a bit. Mostly thinking about the invariant that: if we have two conflicting checkpoints being finalised, then their 2/3 quorums are only guaranteed to share 1/3 stake, if both of their sets mostly overlap If validators are exited immediately, I'm not sure that this invariant holds Maybe we shouldn't immediately exit validators. As long at least ~70% of validators have registered PQ keys, the network should be functional. Seeing low participation would look bad, but it shouldn't really matter. Participation would go back to normal (99%+) after a few weeks/months. There would be an even greater incentive to register PQ keys because those that don't are going to lose quite a bit of stake due to penalties. <@427491045308235776> I just pushed this commit: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/commit/8b7ba37865b5e3b9df689dfa041a92467c17cf0d haven't looked at the above, general comment is i think we need to separate withdrawal delay from validator set churn here. keeping funds locked doesn’t preserve quorum overlap if we immediately remove that stake from the active set, maybe we could schedule non PQ validators through normal exit churn, ideally starting before the fork

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
Ah I see, I need to think through a bit. 

Mostly thinking about the invariant that: if we have two conflicting checkpoints being finalised, then their 2/3 quorums are only guaranteed to share 1/3 stake, if both of their sets mostly overlap

If validators are exited immediately, I'm not sure that this invariant holds

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: Maybe we shouldn't immediately exit validators. As long at least ~70% of validators have registered PQ keys, the network should be functional. Seeing low participation would look bad, but it shouldn't really matter. Participation would go back to normal (99%+) after a few weeks/months. There would be an even greater incentive to register PQ keys because those that don't are going to lose quite a bit of stake due to penalties.
